title: Data Warehousing in Fabric: Microsoft Fabric Tutorial Series
summary: A tutorial-style community post walking through building a Fabric Warehouse Gold layer with CTAS and MERGE patterns, migrating off a Synapse dedicated SQL pool, and modeling conventions for star-schema fact/dimension tables.
audience: Data engineers building their first Fabric Warehouse Gold layer or migrating an existing Synapse dedicated SQL pool warehouse into Fabric.
why_it_matters: The migration checklist (which Synapse-specific DDL to strip out) and the fact-table cardinality heuristic are concrete, reusable rules of thumb not found in the Learn overview docs, which describe the target state but not the migration path or field-tested modeling heuristics.
takeaways: Migrating a Synapse dedicated SQL pool warehouse into Fabric requires stripping distribution and clustered-columnstore-index DDL, which have no Fabric Warehouse equivalent.
CETAS-export-then-OneLake-shortcut-then-COPY-INTO is the suggested data movement path from Synapse into a Fabric Warehouse.
A wide fact table (the post suggests over roughly 50 columns) is a signal that some columns belong in a dimension table instead.
ABFSS path errors are a common early-stage mistake; the path format needs the workspace and item names in the right positions.

claims.text: Migrating DDL from a Synapse dedicated SQL pool into Fabric Warehouse requires removing distribution clauses (HASH, ROUND_ROBIN, REPLICATE), clustered columnstore index syntax, and manual INDEX REBUILD/REORGANIZE/CREATE STATISTICS statements, none of which have a Fabric Warehouse equivalent.

The suggested path for moving data from a Synapse dedicated SQL pool into Fabric is: CETAS-export the Synapse tables to Parquet in ADLS Gen2, create a OneLake shortcut to that ADLS container, then load into the Fabric Warehouse with COPY INTO.
A practitioner heuristic offered in the post: a fact table with more than roughly 50 columns is likely carrying attributes that should be split out into a dimension table instead.

The post documents error 110802 as caused by an invalid ABFSS path or missing permissions, and recommends verifying the abfss://<workspace>@onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/<item>/... path format as the fix.
The post recommends batching large DML deletes by partition rather than issuing a single large WHERE-clause delete, since very large single-transaction deletes can hit Delta transaction log limits.
The recommended fix for a Direct Lake fallback caused by unsupported T-SQL constructs in a view is to materialize the view and remove non-deterministic functions from its definition.
